examples.title: EV charger in a triple-decker
examples.demonstrates: A tight service that doesn't need an upgrade, because a load manager caps the charger.

checks.title: Service capacity after the new load
checks.message: Calculated load is 97.2 A, 97.2% of the 100 A service. That is within the rating but above PermitPike's 80% planning threshold (not a code limit).
checks.suggestedFix: Confirm the load inputs with the electrician; little headroom is left for future loads. A listed power control system that caps EV charger (40 A) (NEC 2026 120.7, 625.42, Article 130) would keep the calculated load within the 100 A rating.

checks.title: Branch circuit sized for continuous load
checks.message: 50 A breaker is at least 125% of the 40 A charger output (50 A).

checks.message: Spec sheet shows an outdoor-rated (Type 4) enclosure.

checks.title: Energy management system caps the charger
checks.message: A listed energy management system limits the charger so the service is not overloaded.

recommendation.summary: The 100 A service is at 97% with the 40 A charger, which is tight. Recommend approval on the condition that the load manager is set and sealed.

examples.title: Home battery with solar
examples.demonstrates: A failing code check, a field the AI couldn't find and won't guess, and an Eversource interconnection flag.

checks.title: Service capacity after the new load
checks.message: Calculated load is 64.2 A, 32.1% of the 200 A service.

checks.title: Busbar 120% rule for backfed breaker
checks.message: 200 A main + 60 A backfeed = 260 A, over 120% of the 200 A busbar (240 A).
checks.suggestedFix: Limit the backfeed breaker to 40 A, downsize the main breaker, or connect on the supply side.

checks.title: Energy storage system is listed
checks.message: Could not find a UL 9540 listing in the documents. The spec sheet lists UL 1973 for the modules only.
checks.suggestedFix: Upload the UL 9540 certificate or a spec sheet that shows the system listing.

checks.title: Install location and clearance to openings
checks.message: basement install, 6 ft from the nearest opening.

steps.label: General lighting and receptacles: 1,900 sq ft × 2 VA/sq ft
First 8,000 VA of existing load at 100%
15,400 VA ÷ 240 V = 64.2 A on a 200 A service

check.title: Service capacity after the new load
check.message: Calculated load is 64.2 A, 32.1% of the 200 A service.

utilityFlag.reason: Battery is paired with existing solar and can export to the grid.
utilityFlag.action: Submit an Eversource interconnection application; the system cannot operate until approved.

cleanEnergyTip.message: The homeowner may be able to earn incentives by enrolling the battery in Mass Save ConnectedSolutions.

inspectorChecklist: Battery model and UL 9540 label match the approved spec sheet.
Backfeed breaker size matches the approved single-line diagram.
Clearance to doors and windows matches the site plan.
Eversource interconnection approval on file.
recommendation.summary: The 60 A backfeed plus the 200 A main is 260 A, over the 240 A the busbar allows, so this needs a fix. The spec sheet lists UL 1973 for the modules but not the UL 9540 system listing, so we could not confirm it. Because the battery is paired with solar it also needs Eversource interconnection approval. Recommend returning for a smaller backfeed breaker and the UL 9540 certificate.
